720	At the top, the connection between the head and the body is
721	the throat. The throat is
722	the connector: it joins the intellectual part with the
723	animal part, the physical part that man shares
724	with the beast, whose whole purpose is simply, technically,
725	to allow a person to exist. That is, thought, seemingly,
726	could exist only in the head, without the body. But then
727	a person could not bring thought from potential
728	to actual and carry it out. So the carrying out
729	of thought is in the tools of action, the tools of action from the
730	shoulders
731	down. Thought happens in the head. What happens in the connection,
732	the speech? The throat and the mouth, that is
733	speech. Speech is this
734	connection. The three actions, or the three domains of
735	possible
736	human action, and this is an idea that appears in Kabbalah many
737	times: the three fields of action are thought,
738	speech and deed. Deed is the deed of the hands,
739	of the feet, action.
740	Speech is speech,
741	and thought. These are levels, one above
742	the other. Thought is where everything is, that is to say,
743	thought is the most fantastic and most
744	exclusive field, unique to man. Man is able
745	to think, able to understand, able
746	to think. Deed is something man shares with animals.
747	Many of the deeds we do as human beings
748	we do on an instinctive level, like
749	animals. We are also able to do deliberate
750	deeds, meaning that the deed comes after thought
751	first. So there is thought and there is deed. What
752	does the throat connect?
753	Speech. Speech, then, is
754	an amazing tool, unique and exclusive to man. Only human beings
755	speak.
756	I mean intelligent speech. True, dolphins
757	also "speak," and there is also the language of birds, but
758	that is chirping,
759	just sounds, it is not intelligent speech. Intelligent speech
760	is exclusive, it is unique to man. And the uniqueness
761	stems from the fact that only man has
762	a soul, a soul in the higher
763	spiritual sense. Therefore the combination of body and soul is expressed
764	in speech. This is what gives speech
765	immense importance, because, as we said, speech is
766	the garment of
767	thought. If we understand things correctly, we can understand
768	the commandment
769	in the Torah that one must keep
770	one's speech: "That which has gone out of your lips you shall keep
771	and do." "He shall not profane his word." If a person says something and does not
772	fulfill it, this is called profaning the
773	word. Let us explain this expression for a moment. It appears, by the way,
774	in the book of Bamidbar, Parashat Matot, in the laws of vows: "If a man
775	vows a vow to HaShem, he shall not profane his word." What does
776	"profane his word" mean? Not fulfilling it is called
777	profaning it. Let us explain the word "to profane." What
778	is
779	profanation? In the previous parashah, Parashat Ki Tetzê,
780	we learned at the end of the parashah: "If one is found
781	slain, fallen, it is not known who struck him." What is a "challal"? Okay,
782	unfortunately we know this expression
783	too well from the wars of Israel: "chalalim,"
784	fallen soldiers. What is a "challal"? Why is a person who died or
785	was killed called
786	a "challal"? It is also connected to the word
787	"chillul," profanation. Chillul is always a state that is the antithesis of
788	kedushah. Chillul is the opposite of kiddush, sanctification.
789	Desecration of the holy: Shabbat is
790	holy Shabbat. It is forbidden to profane the Shabbat: "Those who profane it shall be put to death."
791	Shabbat desecration. Why is it called "chillul"? The word "chillul"
792	is connected to the word
793	"challal," empty,
794	a void. To make a "challal" is to take something that has content and remove
795	its content from it.
796	That is called
797	chillul. The people of
798	Israel: when the Holy One, blessed be He, chose us from all
799	the nations at Mount Sinai, He sent Moshe Rabbeinu
800	and offered us: "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a
801	holy nation." So I always say jokingly that every Jew
802	is actually a goy, only he has to be a
803	holy goy. "You shall be holy, for I, HaShem, am holy." The people of
804	Israel is a people like all peoples, but it is holy. It has
805	kedushah in it. The antithesis of
806	kedushah is "chiloni," secular. By the way, this expression is a
807	shocking expression that we have all gotten used to using, but
808	for someone who understands its meaning, people
809	speak and do not understand what they are saying. What does it mean
810	to be a Jewish
811	"chiloni"? "Chiloni" comes from the language of "chillul." It
812	means the uprooting of kedushah. I am Jewish, but I do not
813	do anything holy. I do not keep mitzvot,
814	"Who has sanctified us with His commandments." I do not want to be sanctified
815	by His commandments, and I live my life as if I were not
816	Jewish. Now, if a goy lives his life as a non-Jew,
817	fine, he is a goy. But a Jew has
818	the obligation of kedushah. When he removes the
819	kedushah from within himself, he creates
820	a void, the chillul. So a person
821	who is killed, murdered, or whose
822	soul has left him, a void is created, because the central, supreme,
823	spiritual thing that gives him life, "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of
824	life," He gave a breath, a soul of life.
825	The soul gives life to the body. So when this soul
826	departs, a void is created. Therefore a person who fell in battle
827	or in general
828	was murdered, not necessarily in battle, as it says in the Torah: "If one is found
829	slain, fallen in the field, it is not known who struck him." It does not have
830	to be someone who fell in battle. A person from whom
831	his central point has departed, which is
832	the soul. "He shall not profane his word": there is such a thing too. Speech
833	is holy. Whoever understands what we explained about
